decision_rule: Prefer ROLLBACK_REBUILD unless CURRENT_REPAIR is demonstrably smaller, cleaner, and less ambiguous.

benefits: Starts from the proven clean three-method presentation surface.
Leaves the live model.track hybrid orchestration untouched.
Excludes standardized replay and rf_hybrid_offline by construction.
required_forward_ports: Standard V2 evaluator implementation and its contract tests
generic prediction comparison and artifact hashing
all unrelated classification_v2 changes currently on main
integration_risk: The clean base is an ancestor of current main, so preserving current classification_v2 while replacing only tracking requires a nontrivial history integration.
Forward-porting the evaluator and authorities is larger than removing the isolated active-method pollution.
A broad subtree replacement would risk touching unrelated classification_v2.

required_actions: Remove rf_hybrid_offline from the active presentation registry.
Remove the obsolete generic RF offline adapter from production.
Restore an explicit three-method registry and explicit hybrid_bytetrack lineage contract.
Separate detector-cache, B0/B1, 2x2, and historical-recovery runners from production entry points.
Retain Standard V2 and identity-episode evaluators as method-neutral infrastructure.
Rewrite only tests that encode an invalid active-method or standardized-2x2 assumption.
current_repair_assessment.reason: The active pollution is concentrated in one profile, one adapter module, one runner branch, and their metadata bindings. The accepted hybrid lineage and clean three-profile authority are already frozen, so behavior can be restored against named contracts without reconstructing history again.

evidence: Current repair has a 12-file initial production/test allowlist.
Rollback rebuild must forward-port at least 22 evaluator source/test files plus authorities and the entire current classification_v2 tree.
The invalid active method is explicitly named and isolated.
The full accepted hybrid lineage is already recovered and must be bound, not reimplemented from speculative runtime behavior.
